body.en:
Most fastener failures in Zimbabwean mining are not breaking failures; they are eating-away failures. The bolt that sheared would have been specified by the engineer anyway. The bolt that corroded until the nut would not turn, or the plate that thinned at the edge until it stopped holding the rock, was specified by nobody — it was bought from stock.

The reason the corrosion question comes first in this market is the water. Underground workings in sulphide-bearing rock produce acidic water when the rock oxidises, and that water is pumped, stored, sprayed and leaked through the whole circuit. It sits in sumps where pipework flanges live, it wets the ground where rock bolts are installed, and it condenses on steel in the return airways. A fastener in that circuit is in a chemical environment, not a mechanical one.

The surface side has a different version of the same problem. Chrome and platinum operations move abrasive ore and process it with water; mill liner bolts, screen decks and pump flanges see slurry, and slurry is both abrasive and electrically conductive. Add the rainy season, when laterite dust turns into mud that stays wet against steel for weeks, and the corrosion load on the site is continuous rather than occasional.

What that means for selection is a sequence: identify the exposure each item actually sees, choose the protection that survives it, then choose the strength class the load needs. Doing it in the other order — strength first, protection as an afterthought — is how sites end up with correctly rated bolts that fail at the head after two seasons.

The ore body decides the item list, too. Narrow-reef platinum and gold workings are underground hard-rock operations with rock bolts, mesh, rail and ventilation; chrome is open-cast with screens, conveyors and smelter-side handling; lithium pegmatite sits between the two. Each of those has its own short list of fasteners that fail most often, and that short list is where the procurement effort belongs.
body.zh:
津巴布韦矿山里失效的紧固件，多数不是断掉，而是被腐蚀掉。断掉的那根，工程师本来就会选；真正出事的是螺母锈死转不动，或者托盘边缘蚀薄到托不住岩面——这一类根本没人给它做过选型，是从仓库随手领的。

腐蚀问题排在载荷前面，原因在水。含硫化物岩层氧化后产出酸性水，这些水在坑内被抽排、储存、喷洒、渗漏，整条回路都泡着它；泵坑里的法兰、装岩锚杆的底板、回风道的钢件，全都长期处在化学环境里，而不是单纯的受力环境。

地表侧是同一个问题的另一种形态。铬矿和铂矿湿法处理磨蚀性矿石，磨机衬板螺栓、筛板、泵法兰长期接触矿浆，矿浆既磨蚀又导电；再加上雨季红土粉尘变成泥，贴着钢件湿上几周。现场的腐蚀载荷是连续的，不是偶发的。

所以选型顺序应当是：先看这一件东西实际处在什么暴露条件，再选能活下来的防护，最后才定载荷需要的强度等级。反过来做——先定强度、防护事后补——现场就会出现等级完全正确、两个季度后从头部锈断的螺栓。

矿体也决定清单。铂和金的窄脉矿是地下硬岩开采，岩锚杆、网片、轨道、通风；铬矿是露天，筛分、皮带、冶炼侧输送；锂辉石介于两者之间。每类矿体都有几张"最常坏"的紧固件清单，采购的力气应该花在那里。

body.en:
The standards a mine buyer names in the order determine what can be checked at the gate, so they should be few and specific. For the bolt itself, the property class standard is the anchor: it defines the strength class marked on the head, the test loads and the marking that has to be on the product. A bolt without the class marking is unverifiable no matter what the mill certificate says.

For stainless items, the applicable standard defines the alloy groups rather than individual grades, which matters because the site will talk in 304 and 316 while the standard talks in A2 and A4. Naming the alloy group in the order and the grade in brackets prevents the substitution that happens when a supplier runs short.

For galvanising, the hot-dip standard defines coating mass and thickness by class, and the class is what has to be written down. "Galvanised" alone is not a specification: it can mean a coating that survives a warehouse and a coating that survives a sump. For hardware items — nuts, washers, plates — the separate hardware coating standard applies, and the mine should name it rather than inherit whatever the supplier uses.

Mining-specific practice sits on top of these. Rock bolt assemblies, mill liner bolts and crusher hardware are usually bought against a drawing as well as a standard, because the geometry — head type, thread length, washer size — is part of the function. A standard-compliant bolt with the wrong thread length is still the wrong bolt.

The written order should therefore carry four lines per item: strength class, alloy or coating class, the drawing or dimension reference, and the traceability requirement. That is enough for a receiving inspector to reject a wrong delivery, and it is short enough that a supplier cannot claim it was ambiguous.
body.zh:
订单里写哪几个标准，决定了到货时能查什么，所以宜少宜具体。螺栓本体锚定在性能等级标准上：它规定头部打的等级标记、试验载荷和必须标注的内容。没有等级标记的螺栓，材质书再漂亮也无法核对。

不锈钢件要看合金组别标准，而不是单个牌号。现场习惯说 304、316，标准说的是 A2、A4，这中间的差距正好是缺货时被替换的口子。订单里同时写合金组别和括号里的牌号，替换就少了一半空间。

热镀锌要写镀层等级，而不是"镀锌"两个字。锌层可以薄到只够撑过仓库，也可以厚到撑过泵坑，同一个词覆盖这两种东西。螺母、垫圈、托盘这类五金件另有对应的镀层标准，矿山应当点名，不要沿用供应商的默认做法。

矿山专有的做法叠在这几层之上。岩锚杆组件、衬板螺栓、破碎机件通常既要标准也要图纸，因为头型、螺纹长度、垫圈尺寸本身就是功能的一部分。符合标准但螺纹长度不对的螺栓，照样是错的螺栓。

body.en:
Three protection routes compete in this market, and each wins in a different part of the site. Hot-dip galvanising is the workhorse: it is cheap per unit, it protects steel in atmospheric and moderately wet service, and it survives handling and installation without being damaged by a spanner. It loses where the water is acidic or where the item is immersed, because zinc is consumed by acid rather than passivated by it.

High-tensile steel is the strength route: it delivers the class the mill liner or crusher bolt needs, and it is normally supplied galvanised or coated rather than bare. It does not solve a corrosion problem, and a high-tensile bolt in an acidic sump will corrode at exactly the same rate as a mild one — it just fails at a higher load when it does.

Stainless is the immersion route. It wins where the item is permanently wet, where the water is chloride-bearing, or where the fastener cannot be replaced without stopping the circuit. It loses on cost and on strength: standard stainless classes are below the high-tensile classes, so a stainless substitution in a loaded joint is a strength decision disguised as a corrosion decision.

The fourth route is the one sites use most and specify least: a coated carbon steel item with a maintenance regime. It works when the item is accessible — surface pipework, conveyor frames, screen structures — and it fails when the item is buried in a sump or behind a liner. The mistake is to apply a maintenance assumption to an item nobody can reach.

In practice, the split that holds up is by location: underground wet and acidic service goes stainless or heavily coated with a defined class, surface structural and conveyor work goes hot-dip galvanised, and high-load joints go high-tensile with the coating the environment demands.
body.zh:
现场实际在比的是三条防护路线，各自赢在不同位置。热镀锌是主力：单件便宜，能护住大气和中等潮湿环境，装卸和扳手操作都不容易破坏它；但遇到酸性水或浸没工况就输，因为锌是被酸消耗掉的，不是被钝化的。

高强钢走的是强度路线：衬板螺栓、破碎机件需要的等级由它给，通常以镀锌或涂层状态供货。它不解决腐蚀问题——酸性泵坑里的 10.9 和 4.8 腐蚀速度一样，只是断的时候载荷更高。

不锈钢走的是浸没路线。长期湿、含氯、或者停机才能更换的位置，是它的地盘；代价是价格和强度：常规不锈钢等级低于高强等级，在受力接头里把高强换成不锈钢，本质是拿强度换了防腐，不是纯赚。

第四条路线现场用得最多、写得最少：涂层碳钢加维护制度。位置够得着就成立——地表管道、皮带机架、筛分结构；埋在泵坑里、藏在衬板后面就不成立。错误在于把"可维护"这个假设用在没人够得着的地方。

能站住的分法其实按位置切：坑内潮湿酸性工况用不锈钢或写清等级的重涂层；地表结构和输送用热镀锌；高载荷接头用高强钢，再按环境选镀层。

body.en:
Receiving inspection on a mine is a gate check, not a laboratory. It has to be fast, it has to be repeatable by a storeman, and it has to be able to stop a delivery that will cost the plant a shutdown. Four checks do most of that work.

The first is documentation against the order: the mill certificate must reference the heat, the class and the standard named in the purchase order, and the certificate must travel with the actual delivery rather than arrive later by email. A certificate for a different heat is not a certificate.

The second is marking. Head marking, grade marking on stainless, and the manufacturer's identification are what tie the physical item to the paper. If the marking is missing or unreadable, the item is unidentified regardless of its paperwork, and unidentified stock is how a wrong grade ends up in a loaded joint.

The third is dimensional and thread check: a thread gauge on a sample from each carton, and the drawing dimensions on the special items. Thread damage from transport is common on heavy mining fasteners, and a damaged thread that gets installed becomes a nut that cannot be removed in five years.

The fourth is coating. On galvanised items, the coating thickness or mass check is the one that catches the delivery that was plated rather than hot-dipped. It is a small bench check and it is worth doing on every batch, because the difference is invisible until the item is in service. Packing condition belongs in the same step: sea freight plus inland haulage to a mine is a long, wet, dusty journey, and a delivery that arrives with broken cartons and no packing list has already lost traceability.

Whatever fails these checks should be quarantined rather than accepted with a note. On a mine, an accepted-but-flagged delivery becomes site stock, and site stock is what gets used at three in the morning.

矿山到货检验是闸口检查，不是实验室。它要快、要仓管员能重复做、要能拦下一批会让选厂停机的货。四道检查干了大部分活。

第一道是单据对订单：材质书要能对上炉号、等级和采购订单里写的标准，而且要跟货一起到，不能事后发邮件补。炉号不对的材质书，不算材质书。

第二道是标记。头部等级标记、不锈钢的牌号标记、制造商标识，是把实物和纸面对上的唯一线索。标记缺失或看不清，这批货在纸面上再全也是身份不明——身份不明的库存，就是错等级混进受力接头的入口。

第三道是尺寸和螺纹：每箱抽一件过螺纹规，专用件按图纸量。重型矿用紧固件运输中磕伤螺纹很常见，装上去的时候没人管，五年后拆不下来就是它。

第四道是镀层。镀锌件测锌层厚度或重量，是唯一能抓出"电镀冒充热镀"的检查，台面小工具就够，每批都值得做——这个差别在服役前是看不出来的。包装状态算在同一步：海运加内陆长途到矿区，又湿又脏，到货时箱子散了、装箱单没有，追溯其实已经断了。

body.en:
The questions that separate a real supplier from a broker are not about price. They are about whether the same item will arrive the same way next quarter, and whether the supplier can prove what it shipped.

The first question is about coating specification: not "do you galvanise" but which class, to which standard, and whether the coating is verified per batch. A supplier who answers with a class and a test method is a supplier who understands the item; one who answers "good quality" is selling a commodity.

The second is traceability: can the delivery be tied to heats, and can the certificate be reissued for a batch delivered two years ago? Mining consumables are reordered for the life of the ore body, and a supplier who cannot reproduce a batch is a supplier who will silently change something.

The third is range and kit. A mine buys rock bolt assemblies, liner bolts, screen hardware and pipework fasteners on the same requisition, and a supplier who can only supply one line forces the site into three purchase orders and three inspection regimes. Assembly supply — bolt, nut, washer, plate as one item — also removes the mismatch risk that appears when components are bought separately.

The fourth is candour about certification. A supplier who states plainly what certification it holds, and what it can arrange per order, is more useful than one who claims everything. On the buyer's side, this means the specification should ask for what is actually needed — a batch-level material certificate and a dimensional report are usually sufficient — rather than a certificate the supplier cannot legitimately issue.

The fifth is logistics to an inland destination. Zimbabwe is served through Beira and Durban, and the last leg is road; a supplier who has quoted the packing, the documents and the transit time for that route has priced the delivery that actually happens, not the one on the drawing.

第一个问题是镀层怎么写：不是"你们镀不镀锌"，而是哪个等级、按哪个标准、每批是否验证。答得出等级和检测方法的，是懂这件东西的人；答"质量很好"的，卖的是大宗货。

第二个是追溯：这批货能不能对上炉号，两年前发的批能不能补开材质书。矿用易耗件要跟着矿体寿命反复补货，重现不了一批货的供应商，就会在某一次悄悄换掉里面的东西。

第四个是对认证的坦白。说清楚自己持有什么、哪些能按订单协助办，比什么都敢答的更有用。买方这一侧同样要把要求写成真正需要的东西：批次材质书加尺寸报告通常就够，不必强求一张供应商根本没资格开具的证书。

第五个是到内陆点的物流。津巴布韦走贝拉和德班两个口，最后一段是陆运；把包装、单证和这段在途时间都算进报价的供应商，报的是真的会发生的交付，不是图纸上的交付。

body.en:
Mine procurement teams tend to ask the same handful of questions, and the answers are usually about how the item will be bought rather than what it is.

The most common is whether one grade can cover the whole site. It cannot, because the site contains sumps, conveyors and loaded joints, and those three need three different answers. The second is whether stainless is worth the cost; it is where the item is immersed and inaccessible, and it is not worth it on surface frames that can be repainted.

The third is how to specify galvanising without writing a standard the local supplier cannot meet. The answer is to name the class and let the supplier meet it, and to verify the coating on arrival rather than on the invoice. The fourth is what to do when the certificate is missing; the practical answer is to quarantine the batch, because an unidentified batch on a mine has a way of becoming installed stock.

See frequently asked questions below.
